title: Dhol (Punjabi barrel drum)
summary: The dhol is a big, loud, two-headed barrel drum of Punjab and the lands around it. It hangs from a strap and is struck with two different sticks: a thick curved stick on the large bass head and a thin cane on the small bright head, together giving the driving beat of bhangra.
howToPlay: The thick stick plays the large head: Dagga is the deep stroke. The thin cane plays the small head: Tilli is the bright, quick stroke.
Rim is a click on the edge of the bass head, and Shell is a knock on the wood.
A ring closes on a place when its stroke is due. Strike as the ring meets the skin.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of bhangra dhol playing, not transcriptions.
heritageNote: The dhol leads the dancing at weddings and harvest gatherings across Punjab. Its steady two-stick pattern is the heartbeat of bhangra.
